title.narrative: Urban Water Supply and Sanitation Sector Project (UWSSSP)

description.narrative:
The project will improve access to safe water and improved sanitation in urban and peri-urban areas of Solomon Islands. The population of Solomon Islands is currently estimated at 642,000 and is growing at approximately 1.9% annually. About 152,000 (24%) of the Solomon Islands population live in urban and peri-urban areas, the largest of which is greater Honiara, with an estimated population of about 105,000. Based on medium growth projections, Solomon Islands urban population may grow to 430,000 by 2050. The population of greater Honiara is expected to surpass 300,000 within the next 30 years.


The overall objective of UWSSSP is to increase access to safe water and improved sanitation in urban areas.

The UWSSSP specific objective targets improved efficiency, climate change and disaster resiliency, and sustainability of safe water and sanitation in the greater Honiara area and other five urban areas (Auki, Gizo, Munda, Noro, and Tulagi)

 All objectives are aligned with the Solomon Islands Government (SIG) Medium Term Strategy Objective 3: ¿All Solomon Islanders have access to quality social services, including education and health¿.

description.narrative: UWSSSP targets improved efficiency, climate change and disaster resiliency, and sustainability of safe water and sanitation in the greater Honiara area and other five urban areas (Auki, Gizo, Munda, Noro, and Tulagi).Activities, include strengthening SIWA demand management capacity and optimization of water supply network operations, detection of leaks and illegal connections, repair of leaks or replacement of dilapidated sections of water main, etc.The project is aligned with the goals of: (i) EUs Water, sanitation and Hygiene Policy (May 2014); (ii) the United Nations Security Council Water Diplomacy Conclusions particularly in relation to human rights to safe drinking water and sanitation and commitment to progress on SDG; and (iii) the 11th EDF to support Solomon Islands for water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) and to expand WASH activities to urban areas.
